For a case with G labelled relevant passages and a fixed retrieval depth k, Precision@k = relevant retrieved/k has ceiling min(G,k)/k, whereas Recall@k = relevant retrieved/G has ceiling min(G,k)/G.
Consequently, increasing k can increase attainable recall while decreasing the precision ceiling.
MRR@k and ideal-normalized nDCG@k have ceiling 1 when the corresponding ideal ordering is attainable.
Per-case F1@k has ceiling 2 min(G,k)/(G+k).
These ceilings describe the annotation and retrieval-depth design, not an intrinsic limit of clinical relevance or a model-performance excuse.
Ceiling-normalizing precision is not used to replace conventional precision; with G <= k, it would reproduce recall rather than provide independent evidence of improvement.
No empirical clinical threshold of 0.8 is justified for BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE or BERTScore.
A valid paraphrase need not approach a lexical-overlap ceiling, and a fluent but unsafe answer may have high semantic similarity.
All-case generation metrics also depend on release coverage; withheld cases cannot be removed without reporting the conditional denominator.
Relevance annotations are not exhaustive clinical judgments, so an unlabelled but valid passage can be counted as a false positive under exact-ID scoring.

### 13.15 BMJ paper-inspired Boruta and sensitivity-first forest comparison
Kainth et al. [23] report a Boruta/Random Forest EOS model developed on 2,924 neonates with 548 culture-positive outcomes, with a separate 147-neonate validation cohort.
Their public repository provides training code but no supplied fitted model or original study cohort.
The local comparison therefore adapts the approach to available features rather than reproducing the published model or externally validating its weights.
Original maternal/clinical, centre and pre-suspicion device-exposure inputs are not fabricated.

The adaptation uses BorutaPy 0.4.3 with 1,000 shallow selection trees and a 30-iteration cap, one latest training observation per infant, and training-only absolute Pearson correlation pruning above 0.7.
This differs from R Boruta; repository calls also specify 10,000 trees and 2,000 runs, whereas the paper prose describes 1,000 trees.
Final forests use 120 trees, maximum depth 8 and up to five split candidates.
Training-only class-balanced infant-normalized loss weights replace ROSE oversampling, preserving mixed Kaggle labels without inventing an infant-level outcome.
All-feature unbalanced and balanced forests are controls.
Three forest seeds share fixed patient splits and one selector per fit fold; this is forest-randomization stability, not independent clinical replication.
Kaggle retains the original patient-disjoint fit, threshold and test partitions, leaving the original calibration partition unused.
PIC retains three original patient-level outer folds, reserving threshold-selection infants within each outer training fold.
Only three or four positive infants remain for fitting and one positive infant per threshold set.
Thresholds maximize specificity while attaining at least 90% sensitivity on threshold patients only; held-out outcomes never select or revise the threshold.
